- If sentiment is consistently positive or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative or shows recent decline, model often overcorrects upward; adjust downward bias, especially after sharp spikes.
- After a strong upward spike in history (e.g., >95), model frequently overshoots and fails to account for mean reversion; apply downward correction in 5–10 day horizon.
- When sentiment is flat or near-zero, model often fails to capture volatility or mean reversion; use smoother trend or add volatility buffer.
- If true outcome shows early sharp drop after high peak, model may not recognize “sell-off” sentiment; reduce forecast slope after peak, especially if sentiment turns negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often assumes linear continuation; if sentiment shows divergence from trend, introduce early correction or adjust horizon-specific decay.
